'''Steven Scott Gubser''' (May 4, 1972 – August 3, 2019) was a professor of [[physics]] at [[Princeton University]].<ref name=PrincetonProfile/> His research focused on theoretical particle physics, especially [[string theory]], and the [[AdS/CFT correspondence]]. He was a widely cited scholar in these and other related areas.<ref name=GoogleScholar/>

Gubser did foundational work in the [[AdS/CFT correspondence]] as a graduate student. In particular, his 1998 paper ''Gauge Theory Correlators from Non-Critical String Theory'' with his advisor [[Igor Klebanov]] and another Princeton physics professor [[Alexander Markovich Polyakov]], made a precise statement of the [[AdS/CFT]] duality. It is one of the all-time top cited papers in theoretical high-energy physics, and is commonly known, along with [[Edward Witten]]'s 1998 work ''Anti De Sitter Space And Holography'', as the GKPW dictionary. After receiving a Ph.D. in 1998 from Princeton, Gubser became a [[Harvard Society of Fellows|junior fellow]] at [[Harvard University]] before taking a position as an assistant professor at Princeton. In 2001, he moved to the [[California Institute of Technology]] but returned to Princeton in 2002.<ref name=GuggenheimProfile/> Gubser's later works concern various aspects of the [[AdS/CFT correspondence]], including its applications in [[quantum chromodynamics]] and [[condensed matter physics]]. In 2016 he and collaborators proposed a [[p-adic number|p-adic]] version of [[AdS/CFT correspondence]] whose bulk geometry is a tree graph. 

As a high school student in 1989, Gubser was the first American to be grand winner (ranked first among all gold medalists) of the [[International Physics Olympiad]].<ref name=AT060218/><ref name=NT890815/> He graduated from [[Cherry Creek High School]] in [[Greenwood Village, Colorado]]. 

He graduated as the [[valedictorian]] of the class of 1994 from Princeton University. For his senior thesis he was awarded the LeRoy Apker Award of the American Physical Society, the highest distinction for undergraduate research. 

==Awards==
* 1994 [[LeRoy Apker Award]] for outstanding undergraduate achievement from the [[American Physical Society]]<ref name=ApkerAward/>
* 2008 [[Blavatnik Awards for Young Scientists|Blavatnik Award]] of the [[New York Academy of Sciences]]<ref name=MNT081119/><ref name="NYAS2008" />
* 2009 [[Guggenheim Fellowship]]<ref name=GuggenheimProfile/>
* 2011 [[Gribov Medal]] of the [[European Physical Society]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=High Energy and Particle Physics Division of EPS |title=Gribov Medal |url=https://eps-hepp.web.cern.ch/other-prize-awards.php |access-date=2026-02-07 |website=eps-hepp.web.cern.ch}}</ref>
* 2017 [[Simons Investigator]]<ref name=SimonsAward/>

== Personal life & death ==
Gubser was married to [[Laura Landweber]], and they had three daughters.<ref name="NYT20190906">{{cite news | title=Steven Gubser, a Bright Star in the Physics Universe, Dies at 47 | work=[[The New York Times]] | first=Dylan Loeb | last=McClain | date=September 6, 2019 | url=https://www.nytimes.com/2019/09/06/science/steven-gubser-dead.html | access-date=September 7, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine | first=Abigail | last=Jeffries | title=Ingenious, Innovative, and Interdisciplinary! | magazine=The New York Academy of Sciences Magazine | url=https://www.nyas.org/magazines/autumn-2008/ingenious-innovative-and-interdisciplinary/ | access-date=September 7, 2019 | pages=11–18 | issue=2, ''Autumn 2008''| year=2008}}</ref>

Gubser died in a rock climbing accident in [[Chamonix]], France, on August 3, 2019.<ref name="LM190805" /><ref name="Princeton190806" /><ref name="NYT20190906" /> Gubser was climbing Aiguille du Peigne "Comb Needle" on the [[Mont Blanc massif]], when a rope broke and he fell to his death.<ref>{{Cite news |last=McClain |first=Dylan Loeb |date=2019-09-06 |title=Steven Gubser, a Bright Star in the Physics Universe, Dies at 47 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2019/09/06/science/steven-gubser-dead.html |access-date=2024-08-05 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>
